title: In an abelian category the map from the coimage A/Ker f to the target of f is a monomorphism
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $f:A\to B$ a morphism of $\mathcal A$, with kernel $\ker f\hookrightarrow A$ and coimage $\mathrm{Coim}(f)=A/\ker f=\mathrm{coker}(\ker f\to A)$, $\pi:A\to A/\ker f$ the projection. Since $f$ vanishes on $\ker f$, $f=\bar f\circ\pi$ for a unique $\bar f:A/\ker f\to B$; then $\bar f$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Definition Tag 0109 (label definition-abelian-category, line 608): in an abelian category the natural map Coim(f) -> Im(f) is an isomorphism, and Im(f) = Ker(B -> Coker f) -> B is a monomorphism, so Coim(f) -> B is a monomorphism
